subject: society
topic: The name on a résumé changes who gets called back
angle: While some gender biases have been eliminated or reversed, hiring discrimination based on race, age, disability, and physical attractiveness remains severe and varies significantly by country and job skill level.
title: The Gatekeepers of the Resume

hooks.text: Who decides if you get the job?
You think gender bias is the main hurdle. It is not.
You are letting a name decide your future.
A cursor blinks on a blank application.

reveal.headline: Discrimination against the elderly and disabled is as severe as racial bias.
reveal.body: Research shows that hiring discrimination against candidates with disabilities, older candidates, and less physically attractive candidates is as severe as treatment based on racial or ethnic characteristics.

explain.headline: Your name and traits determine your callback rate.
explain.body: Evidence confirms that names and characteristics associated with race, age, and disability result in fewer callbacks. This discrimination is significantly greater for low-skilled jobs.

matters.headline: The gatekeepers see you as a category.
matters.body: That may be why your resume feels like a lottery. Your identity might be filtering you out before a human ever sees your skills.

example.headline: A screen glows in a dark room.
example.body: You sit at your desk at 10 pm. You click send on an application. You wait for a notification that may never come because of a name on a page. You are a data point in a filter you cannot see.

verdict: The evidence confirms that names and characteristics associated with race, age, and disability continue to result in fewer callbacks for many applicants.
caveat: The studies show that the level of discrimination varies significantly depending on the specific country, job type, and the amount of positive information provided in the application.
caption:
Your identity acts as a filter before you ever enter the room.

Research shows that discrimination based on race, age, disability, and physical attractiveness remains severe. These biases vary by country and job skill level, with discrimination being significantly higher for low-skilled roles.

Have you ever felt like your resume was being screened by a ghost?
